title: SearchMaster: Grounded and Regulated Self-Play for Search Agents

visual_explainer.question: How does SearchMaster turn self-play task generation itself into a controlled learning problem for search depth and tool-use quality?
visual_explainer.takeaway: The key delta is not self-play alone: explicit evidence-chain task generation, search-depth-aware task reward, and an over-opening penalty shape which tasks and trajectories become training signal.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Naive same-pipeline self-play using success-rate difficulty, plus prior search-agent self-play that does not jointly control evidence-chain grounding, search depth, and opening behavior.

analysis.tldr: SearchMaster treats self-play supervision as a first-class search-agent design problem: it generates evidence-chain-grounded tasks, rewards tasks whose easiest successful solution still needs multiple searches, penalizes over-opening, and jointly trains proposer/solver behavior with GRPO.
analysis.problem: Search-agent self-play can collapse into pseudo multi-hop questions, difficulty signals that reward shallow tasks, and trajectories that open many documents without targeted evidence acquisition. More synthetic data is not automatically useful search supervision.
analysis.core_idea: Use one shared policy as Proposer and Solver in a local search environment, but regulate the self-play loop with Evidence-Chain Generation (ECG), Search-Depth Reward (SDR), an Over-Opening Penalty (OOP), frozen verification, and GRPO over verified proposer/solver rollouts.
analysis.agent_loop: seed document → proposer builds evidence chain and task → filters/verifier → solver search rollouts → correctness + search-depth + opening rewards → joint GRPO update → repeat
analysis.retrieval_design: The deployed search policy uses search/open/find tools over a retrieval environment. The main research object is training-signal construction: task generation and trajectory selection are shaped so that learned search behavior remains evidence-grounded, multi-step, and less opening-heavy.
analysis.evidence: Using the same Qwen3.5-9B backbone, SearchMaster raises average accuracy across six deep-search benchmarks from 38.19% to 51.52%, including 30.12% to 60.24% on BrowseComp-Plus. On BrowseComp-Plus, naive self-play reaches 45.18%; ECG alone 53.25%, SDR alone 52.89%, ECG+SDR 57.71%, and full SearchMaster 60.24%. Separate analyses show higher true multi-hop task rates, sustained search depth, and reduced over-opening behavior.
analysis.why_it_matters: This expands the learning axis beyond 'which retrieval action should the policy take?' to 'which tasks and trajectories should exist as supervision?'. For self-improving search agents, the training distribution and reward semantics can be as causal as the inference-time controller.
limitations: Training is computationally heavy: many proposer/solver rollouts plus frozen-verifier calls are required for each retained seed.
Most external systems in the headline table are not controlled same-backbone/harness baselines; the strongest causal evidence comes from the internal naive-self-play and component ablations.
Training occurs in a large local corpus and evaluation uses a long-context scaffold without context management, so robustness to different search environments and harnesses remains open.
